# Embassy 4.1.0 — the operator's terminal

4.1 adds one command and changes nothing underneath: `embassy tui`, a live terminal view of the broker for the person running it.

**What it shows** — broker health with the ledger revision and the local host name; every registered endpoint with its queue depth and last operation; recent deliveries newest first, with a count of real faults in the tab and success rows shown plainly; retirements; the remote hosts in your `nodes.json` with the age of their last catalog observation. When the broker is unreachable the screen says so first and points at `embassy service status`; a stale view stays visibly stale.

**What it does** — the existing operator verbs from the same screen: refresh discovery, run the loopback check, look up a delivery by token, retire the selected local endpoint. Retirement asks for confirmation on a screen that shows the endpoint's full ID, its provider, queue and last operation, and the settlement consequences, and it refuses to confirm in a terminal too narrow to display the ID. Remote endpoints are never retired from here; the screen names the owning host. Actions never replay; an uncertain outcome is shown with the same hint the CLI prints.

**What it never shows** — message bodies, native session identities, or anything `status --json` does not already expose. It is a pure client: no new broker state, protocol, dependency, or background process. Without an interactive terminal it prints the status text once and exits. It works over ssh in a small window.

**Also in 4.1** — the synchronous-send conformance test no longer depends on a 10 ms scheduling window (the one intermittent failure seen on the 4.0.0 release run), and the CLI and Codex client metadata derive their version from a single constant.

**Upgrading from 4.0.0** — install and restart the broker; no state reset. From 3.x, follow the reset-only procedure in the 4.0.0 notes.

**Tested with** (m5dev and this-mac, 2026-09-06): the TUI driven against the live 4.0.0 brokers on both machines through a pseudo-terminal, plus two independent operator-perspective reviews whose findings shaped this release; offline suite 338/338.
